question.problem:
$$
B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 1 \\ 4 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

The matrix $B$ has eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=5,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=-3,$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=2.$
Find a diagonal matrix $D$ and an invertible matrix $P$ such that $D={P}^{-1}BP.$
question.worked_solution:
We apply the diagonalization algorithm.

**Step 1.**  Notice that we are already given the eigenvalues of the matrix: 

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}=5,\,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=-3,\,$ ${\lambda }_{3}=2.$ 

**Step 2.** Now, we need to find an eigenvector basis of $A.$ Applying our usual method, we get the following.

- For ${\lambda }_{1}=5,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}B-5I & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 4 & 1 \\ 4 & -4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(B-5I)x=0$ gives us the eigenvector ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}=-3,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}B-(-3)I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 4 & 1 \\ 4 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(B-(-3)I)x=0$ gives us the eigenvector ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

- For ${\lambda }_{3}=2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}B-2I & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 & 1 \\ 4 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(B-2I)x=0$ gives us the eigenvector ${v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$

**Step 3.** We construct the diagonal matrix $D$ and the invertible matrix $P$ in the usual way, and this gives us the following:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$
